findings.reason: the plan's own sequencing is the only route to an implementable section, so without a followup naming §16 (or §16 added to f-amfc-004's body) the section is orphaned and will not be dispatched; the author has acted on this same class of finding three times already for §8/§9/§10/§11.
findings.text: §16 is added to plan-section-declarations as `implementable` (plan.html:24, `"s16":"implementable"`), but the only open followup, f-amfc-004, recommends `/reckon-build an-mcp-failure-names-its-cause §13` and neither its body nor its prompt names §16, so no followup drives the new section and the plan's declared next invocation builds §13 and stops

findings.reason: the mechanism does not remove the double-write the section exists to prevent, because the field the caller reads for advice still instructs a retry; the author should extend the deliverable to the hint (or state that the message supersedes it), and the done-when should assert the hint as well.
findings.text: the section's Why states the harm is "The result's hint says to retry once storage recovers, so a caller following it would have written each landing twice", but the Deliverable changes only "the message"; `_STORAGE_SLOW_HINT` in `reckon/_mcp_tools.py:16` is unmodified and is still returned as `hint` for a write whose `cause` is `waiting`, so a write that now reports `landed: None` still carries the advice "Retry once the storage recovers"

rubric_items.done_when: pass — §16's three-body done-when is measurable and names a real negative control (restoring today's "False whenever the grace ends with the file unchanged" reddens the in-flight body), with the control logged under the run directory.
rubric_items.evidence_paths: pass — §16 places its control log under the run directory, the plan's existing convention (§13, §15), not a scratchpad or node-local temporary path.
rubric_items.naming: pass — §16 names the mechanism (`test_a_write_in_flight_is_not_reported_unlanded.py`, `_landing_state`, `_InflightBody`); no plan labels, stage names, ticket numbers or changelog prose.
rubric_items.reasoning: a finding — §16's Why names the retry hint as how the double-write happens, but its Deliverable changes only the message, leaving that hint in place.
rubric_items.single_goal: pass — §16 carries one deliverable: a timed-out write whose body is still running reports `landed: None` rather than `False`.
